newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil sentiment stays firm on winter demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil sentiment stays firm on winter demand.

text.p: NWE fuel oil markets remained firm despite weak crude as winter demand in Europe and the United States remained firm.
News that a new oil-fired power station in Brindisi, Italy is due to come on stream in early December merely confirmed traders' already bullish outlook.

Low sulphur cargoes at $132 fob NWE were at their highest level ever, except for a short period during the Gulf War, but traders thought the rally was not yet finished. Said one: "They are very high but it doesn't mean they can't go higher."

Traders were unclear if Italy would continue to buy cargoes for Dec, having picked up around 250,000 tonnes last week, because congestion in Italian ports had already created delays of up to three weeks.

High sulphur cargoes were still in strong demand from the U.S. and natural gas prices extended their rally on Monday. Two traders were talking around $119-120 cif NWE for a prompt high sulphur cargo, and fob prices were steady around $113-114. High sulphur barges rose $3 to trade at $117-121 fob ARA.
